name: Frozen — Movie Companion
description: Pause-and-talk cards for family movie night with Frozen (2013). Each item is one pause point: a Wonder Together question for the kid, a For the Grown-up note, and an optional tap-quiz (metadata.quiz). metadata.time is where it fires (ad-free version, approximate — use the extension's nudge buttons); metadata.lens is the theme — "discussion" or "repair" (rupture → armor → truth → return → restoration). Our own commentary and questions only — no film dialogue, lyrics, or studio artwork. Part of the Family Watch Club (watch.recursive.eco).

attribution.note: Commentary about the film. Contains no film dialogue, lyrics, or studio artwork. Scene titles reference song/scene names for navigation only.

sections.Wonder Together: The trolls say the head can be persuaded, but the heart is harder. What do you think that means?
sections.For the Grown-up: The whole movie is set up in this one line of folk wisdom. Notice what the grown-ups do with the warning: they erase Anna's memory and hide Elsa away — they treat a HEART problem with a HEAD solution. Watch how that works out.

options.reply: That's what we might hope — but watch again. The gates close, the staff is reduced, the gloves go on...

options.text: Hide them — gloves, closed gates, secrets
options.reply: YES. They choose hiding over practicing. It comes from love AND fear at once — and it becomes the armor Elsa carries for the whole movie.
No — they keep her home. But home becomes a kind of hiding place.

quiz.question: What do the parents decide to do about Elsa's powers?

items.name: Do You Want to Build a Snowman?

sections.Wonder Together: Anna knocks and knocks for years. Why doesn't Elsa ever open the door?
sections.For the Grown-up: Repair-arc reading: the closed door is armor, not rejection — Elsa believes staying away IS the loving thing. Both sisters are hurting on opposite sides of the same door, each thinking the other doesn't want them. Worth asking: has anyone ever seemed to shut you out when they were really protecting you?

options.reply: She loves her the WHOLE time — watch her face on the other side of the door.

options.text: She's scared of hurting Anna again
options.reply: YES. The door is armor around an old accident. Protection that outlived its moment — Moana's dad has the same rule about the reef.
This is years before she's queen. It started the night of the accident.

quiz.question: Why does Elsa keep the door closed?

sections.Wonder Together: Anna wants to marry Hans the day she met him! What do you think about that?
sections.For the Grown-up: The movie deliberately sets up the fairy-tale shortcut so it can question it later. A kid-sized way in: how long does it take to really know a friend? Anna has been lonely behind closed gates for years — the loneliness, not silliness, is what makes the shortcut tempting.

options.text: Because Hans is definitely her true love
options.reply: The movie has a BIG surprise about that. Keep watching...

options.text: Because she's been lonely for so long
options.reply: YES. Years of closed doors made an open door feel like everything. Loneliness can make us decide too fast.

options.text: Because the trolls told her to
options.reply: The trolls aren't here — this one is all Anna.

quiz.question: Why does Anna say yes so fast?

sections.Wonder Together: Elsa finally uses her powers and builds something beautiful. Is she free now, or alone — or both?
sections.For the Grown-up: The trick of this scene: it FEELS like pure victory, and it's half of one. Elsa drops the armor of hiding — real progress — but swaps it for the armor of distance (a palace with no door handles, on a mountain, alone). Same tension as Moana's ocean and Rumi's stage: the truth is out, but connection still missing.

options.reply: It IS beautiful. But count the people in it...
YES. She traded hiding-among-people for shining-alone. Free AND lonely can be true at the same time.

quiz.question: Elsa builds an amazing ice palace. What's missing from it?

sections.Wonder Together: Anna climbs a whole frozen mountain to reach her sister. What makes her keep going?
sections.For the Grown-up: Repair-arc: this is the RETURN step — going toward the person instead of away. Notice it doesn't work yet: Anna returns, but leads with the problem (the frozen kingdom), and Elsa's armor slams down harder. Return alone isn't enough; the truth step hasn't happened yet. Real repairs often take more than one try.

options.text: Anna doesn't really want to fix things
options.reply: She climbed a MOUNTAIN for this. Wanting isn't the problem.

options.text: Elsa's fear rises faster than Anna's words can land
options.reply: YES. When armor is threatened it strikes out — Elsa literally storms. You can't reason with armor; the hurt under it has to be spoken to. First tries at repair often fail. Keep watching.
Olaf is actually the most honest one on that mountain!

quiz.question: Anna reaches Elsa at last — why does it go wrong?

sections.Wonder Together: Only an act of true love can thaw a frozen heart. What counts as an act of true love?
sections.For the Grown-up: Everyone in the movie — and most of us watching — assumes it means a kiss someone GIVES you. The ending flips it: the act of true love is one Anna DOES. Pause here and collect guesses; the wrong guesses are the fun part.

sections.Wonder Together: Anna could run to her kiss and save herself. She turns toward Elsa instead. Why?
sections.For the Grown-up: The whole repair arc lands here. Anna's act says the truth out loud better than words: you are worth standing in front of. And watch what it unlocks — Elsa finally learns the counter-rule to the one she was raised on: not conceal-don't-feel, but love as the thing that makes power safe. Repair that re-equips, exactly like Te Fiti restoring Maui's hook.

options.reply: Ouch — the movie has other plans for Hans.
Close guess — the movie WANTS you to think that. But Anna never reaches him...

options.text: Anna putting herself between the sword and Elsa
options.reply: YES. The act of true love isn't received — it's GIVEN, by the person we thought needed saving. Love turned outward, not a kiss arriving.

quiz.question: What is the act of true love that saves the day?

sections.Wonder Together: At the end, Elsa makes an ice rink for everyone and the gates stay open. What changed — her powers, or something else?
sections.For the Grown-up: Her powers are identical in the first scene and the last. What changed is the rule she lives by — fear says conceal, love says connect. Master lesson, same as Moana's father: who you are is a choice, not a fixed thing, and the people around you can change their rules too. Closing couch question: is there a door in our family that could open a little more?
